test_title: SSC MTS Previous Year Paper (Held on: 20 July 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.

They left the car by __the aside of the road and venture toward__ the forest.

options.text: the side of the road and ventured into
the alongside of the road and ventured to
an aside of road and ventured to

solution:
The correct answer is** "the side of the road and ventured into"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given options, the correct answer is** 'the side of the road and ventured into'.**
 
• Here, adverb **"aside"** needs to be replaced by **"the side"**.
 
• The above sentence is in** simple past tense**, so **"ventured**" is to be used.
 
• We used **"into"** in the sentence to indicate the movement.
 
• Thus,*** option 1) ***is the correct alternative.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Let us understand the usage of the adverbs more clearly.

 
• The directional adverb **"aside"** denotes movement or a shift in position.

 
 
• **Example: **Move **aside**.

 
 
• I will set this **aside** for now.
 
 
 
 
 
• The phrase "**to the side**" has a similar meaning, but it can also refer to the **fixed position **of one object in reference to another.
 
• **Example:** Legs are said to be **"to the side"** or **"on the side" **because they are obviously fixed in place on the body.
 
• Using **"into"** in a sentence denotes motion; an action is taking place.
 
 
• **Example**: He was wandering **into** the woods.
